newsitem.title: USA: IBM tumbles as analysts cut estimates.
newsitem.headline: IBM tumbles as analysts cut estimates.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp's share price tumbled Wednesday as many analysts cut their earnings estimates for the company following lower profit margins and disappointing hardware revenues in the 1996 fourth quarter.
IBM was off 8-3/4 to 159-1/4 in heavy trading, pulling down the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
Late Tuesday the computer giant reported fourth quarter earnings of $3.93 a share, surpassing the consensus Wall Street estimate of $3.88 but falling short of more optimistic forecasts.
Analysts said several factors boosted earnings, including a lower tax rate and lower-than-expected restructuring costs.
Analysts had been expecting restructuring costs of $300-$400 million and a higher tax rate of about 35 percent.

IBM Chief Financial Officer G. Richard Thoman told analysts late Tuesday that IBM could not get enough employees in Europe to accept voluntary buyout plans, and therefore its fourth quarter restructuring expenses were $200 million.
IBM said its tax rate in the quarter was 29.9 percent. Analysts said the low rate boosted earnings by $0.20-$0.30 a share.

John Jones, a Salomon Brothers analyst, said he shaved his 1997 earnings estimates to $12.90 a share from $13.20. He cited a reduction in gross margins, revenues and continued negative currency impact.

Jones cut his 1997 revenue projections to $81.3 billion from $82.79 billion, with $1 billion of the cut coming from future negative currency impact, and the rest due to lower revenues from mainframes, RS/6000 workstations and storage systems.
"Currency has taken a dramatic swing over the past 45 days," Jones said in a note to clients.
IBM had a lower tax rate in the fourth quarter because it has shifted some manufacturing to lower-ax countries such as Singapore and Malaysia, and due to a one-time benefit from Brazil.

"In the quarter, expectations were very, very high," said Stephen Smith, a PaineWebber analyst. "Obviously, the (earnings) number was helped by the lower-than-expected tax rate and a lower-than-expected charge."
Smith remains concerned going forward about strength in mainframes.
Some analysts said they see a buying opportunity in the sharp drop in IBM's stock.
